subject: financial-literacy
instructions: Use only the fictional or supplied figures. Do not disclose household income, accounts, balances, or spending.
Show computations for fixed items and explain the tradeoff or decision for open items.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain opportunity cost and priorities in your own words and give or identify a valid example.
Use a diagram, model, quotation, data display, map, demonstration, or worked process to show understanding of comparison shopping and unit cost.
Apply contracts subscriptions and warranties in a new realistic situation. Show the process or cite evidence.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, unsafe choice, or design flaw involving advertising and behavioral influence; correct it and explain why.
Connect opportunity cost and priorities with fraud scams and identity protection. Explain how the ideas support, constrain, contrast with, or build on one another.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit project: Complete a simulated major-purchase dossier and consumer-protection plan.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy or quality, and one next question.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated accuracy or fidelity criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated evidence and reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated application or performance criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated checking and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.
